title: WASSCE Further Maths: Calculus (Differentiation & Integration) - Further Mathematics - Differentiation (Product and Chain Rule)
subject: Further Mathematics

questions.explain: Using the product rule, $u=(3x+1)^3$, $u'=9(3x+1)^2$. Let $v=x^{1/2}$, $v'=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}$. $y' = 9(3x+1)^2 \sqrt{x} + (3x+1)^3 \frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}$. Creating a common denominator of $2\sqrt{x}$, we get $\frac{18x(3x+1)^2 + (3x+1)^3}{2\sqrt{x}}$. Factoring out $(3x+1)^2$, this simplifies to $\frac{(3x+1)^2(18x + 3x + 1)}{2\sqrt{x}} = \frac{(3x+1)^2(21x+1)}{2\sqrt{x}}$.
